members.name: orb_pullback_entry_v1
members.thesis: Instead of entering at the ORB breakout level (standard approach), waiting for a pullback to the ORB_high (for longs) or ORB_low (for shorts) after the initial breakout provides a better entry price and higher win rate. The pullback entry works because: (1) it confirms the ORB level as support/resis
entry_long: breakout_confirmed == True (price broke above ORB_high for 3+ bars)
pullback_to_ORB == True (price has pulled back to ORB_high level)
entry_short: breakout_confirmed for shorts (close < ORB_low_15 for 3+ bars)
pullback_to_ORB == True (price pulled back up to ORB_low level)
resistance_test: high touches ORB_low_15 ± 0.05% but close stays below
members.exit_target: 2.0 * ORB_range_15 from ORB_high/low (same target as standard ORB, but better entry = better RR)
members.exit_stop: 0.3 * ORB_range_15 below ORB_high (long) or above ORB_low (short) — tight stop just below the level
filters: pullback entry between 09:35-11:00 IST; pullbacks later in the day are less reliable
ORB breakout direction aligned with NIFTY direction preferred
weaknesses: ~30% of successful ORB breakouts never pull back to the ORB level — they extend immediately, and this strategy misses them entirely
The pullback entry can trigger on what's actually a failed breakout that's reverting through the ORB range; the 'support test' can be a bear trap
Limit order at ORB level may not fill exactly due to rapid price movement; partial fills and slippage at the exact level are common
members.prior_art: Brooks (2009) pullback entries; Bulkowski (2005) on throwback/pullback patterns. Markman (2003) 'Swing Trading' pullback concepts applied to ORB.

members.name: orb_retest_v1
members.thesis: After an ORB breakout, the ORB_high or ORB_low level often gets retested 1-3 hours later as mid-day institutional flow revisits the morning's price discovery zone. When the retest holds (price touches ORB_high/low but doesn't close below/above it), it confirms the level as genuine support/resistance
entry_long: retest_up == True (price retested ORB_high and bounced)
close > ORB_high_15 at retest bar close (level held)
RSI_14 > 40 (not deeply oversold, bounce has energy)
entry_short: retest_down == True (price retested ORB_low and got rejected)
close < ORB_low_15 at retest bar close
members.exit_target: session high at time of retest (for longs) + 0.5 * ORB_range_15 (new leg up expected after retest confirmation)
members.exit_stop: 0.3 * ORB_range_15 below ORB_high (long) or above ORB_low (short)
filters: retests between 10:30-14:00 IST; retests after 14:00 may be end-of-day positioning, not genuine
retest bar volume should be LOWER than breakout bar volume (healthy pullback, not new selling/buying wave)
stock must still be above (long) or below (short) VWAP at retest time
weaknesses: Not all breakouts retest — ~40% of valid breakouts continue without retesting the ORB level, meaning this strategy misses a large portion of profitable ORB moves
Distinguishing a 'healthy retest' from a 'reversal through the level' in real-time is difficult; the 0.3 * ORB_range stop is tight and can be hit by normal volatility at the level
The 1-3 hour delay between breakout and retest means the strategy holds capital idle for extended periods, reducing capital efficiency
members.prior_art: Edwards & Magee (1948) on throwback/pullback to breakout levels; Brooks (2009) on retest entries. Bulkowski (2005) statistics on throwback frequency and reliability.

members.name: orb_failure_trade_v1
members.thesis: Failed ORB breakouts — where price breaks above the 15-min ORB high but then reverses back below ORB_high within 15 bars — are high-probability reversal signals. The failure indicates that breakout buyers are trapped and will be forced to liquidate, creating selling pressure that drives price back t
entry_long: breakout_failed_down == True (price broke below ORB_low then came back above it)
RSI_14 > 40 (momentum turning positive after false breakdown)
entry_short: breakout_failed_up == True (price broke above ORB_high then came back below it)
RSI_14 < 60 (momentum turning negative after false breakout)
members.exit_target: opposite ORB extreme (ORB_high for failed-down longs, ORB_low for failed-up shorts)
members.exit_stop: price re-breaks the failed level (new high beyond breakout high for failed-up shorts) OR 0.4 * ORB_range beyond ORB extreme
filters: failures must occur between 09:30-10:00 IST (within first 30 min of ORB formation); enter on failure confirmation
breakout bar had high volume (> 1.5x avg) AND failure bar has rising volume (trapped traders liquidating)
NIFTY direction opposite to the failed breakout direction (macro context supports the reversal)
weaknesses: Distinguishing a genuine failed breakout from a brief re-test that will re-break is extremely difficult; many 'failures' are just pauses before continuation
The strategy enters AFTER the breakout AND the failure, meaning entry is often 5-10 bps worse than the original ORB level due to the round-trip price action
On strong trend days, what appears as a failed breakout in one direction is actually a setup for a massive breakout in the original direction — the failure is the trap
members.prior_art: Brooks (2009) 'Reading Price Charts Bar by Bar' on failed breakouts; Bulkowski (2005) on chart pattern failures. Similar to Adam Grimes (2012) concept of 'failed patterns as signals'.
